newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles dealt financial blow with downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles dealt financial blow with downgrade.

text.p: LOS ANGELES, Dec 13 - Moody's Investors Service Inc on Friday dealt Los Angeles a financial blow, slashing the city's general obligation bonds rating to reflect the passage of a statewide tax measure that could hurt city revenues.
Moody's said it reviewed and lowered the rating on the city's general obligation bonds to Aa from Aa1.

In a statement, Moody's said the primary reason for the rating downgrades was the reduction in revenue flexibility as a result of Proposition 218, which amended the state Constitution to require voter approval of most tax or fee increases and curtailed the use of many types of assessments.

Tim Lynch, deputy Los Angeles city controller, said the downgrade was not surprising "because it (Proposition 218) has reduced our flexibility." Lynch added, however, that the proposition would have little immediate impact on the city's budget. "It's not a disaster for us," he said of the measure.
In its statement, Moody's warned that the city faced a near-term loss of revenues as a result of Proposition 218.
"Officials' success in dealing with these challenges within the restrictions established by the proposition is essential to the maintenance of these ratings at these levels," Moody's said.

Moody's said a business license tax surcharge generating $11 million a year must be approved by the voters or rolled back. A $20 million annual transfer from the water enterprise to the general rund is at risk, the rating agency said.
The city must also deal with the possible reduction of the $100 million annual transfer from the power enterprise as that system takes steps to become more competitive, Moody's said.
"It's a significant rating change but it's not the end of the world," said Ken Kurtz, a vice president at Moody's.
Moody's is currently reviewing the ratings of other large cities in the state in response to Proposition 218.
